headline: Melbourne Solar Innovation Lets Apartment Dwellers Share Rooftop Power
meta_description: Allume Energy's invention enables multiple apartment residents to share a single rooftop solar system without individual installations or inverters.
summary_short: A Melbourne company has created technology that lets apartment residents share rooftop solar power, removing barriers that have long excluded them from renewable energy.
body:
A Melbourne invention is removing one of renewable energy's biggest obstacles: apartment residents have largely been locked out of rooftop solar because of shared building structures and the cost of individual systems.

Allume Energy has developed technology that changes this. Multiple homes can now draw power from a single rooftop installation without needing separate solar panels or individual inverters for each unit. The solution is elegant in its efficiency—shared infrastructure means lower costs and less redundancy.

For apartment dwellers, this represents real progress toward energy independence. Renters and unit owners who lack dedicated roof access have watched homeowners embrace solar for years. Now, shared rooftop systems powered by Allume's innovation could finally bring that option within reach, making clean energy more genuinely accessible across different housing types.
quick_facts: Melbourne company Allume Energy developed the shared rooftop solar technology
Multiple apartment homes can share one rooftop solar system
No individual inverters or separate installations needed per unit
